preamble: The shift from [ə] to [i] raises and fronts the central mid vowel. It is a regular reflex of Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *ə in Tagalog (*bəli > bilí 'buy'), of Proto-Trique *ə in Copala Triqui, and of Proto-Inuit *ə in the western Inuit languages (*əməq > imiq 'water').

examples.note: Copala merged both central vowels *ə and *ɨ into i; yih is the only Copala word with the sequence yi. Chicahuaxtla keeps yəh.
Greenlandic and Tunumiisut imeq have the same /i/, written e before q.
